title.narrative: Scaling Up: Enabling traders to build and sustain a responsible artisanal gold sector in Côte d’Ivoire

description.narrative: A key challenge to scaling or making responsible sourcing initiatives in the artisanal gold mining sector sustainable is competition from the informal gold trade, largely driven by complex networks of small and large traders.Few initiatives have tried to incorporate traders, as their informality and decentralized sourcing from multiple miners and mine sites, with little transparency or information collected, making due diligence implementation challenging. This, in combination with the lack of incentives or an enabling environment to use formal sales channels, has led most responsible sourcing initiatives to cut traders out of the supply chain and enforce a closed-pipe, single source model.This project will work directly with traders as a pathway for scaling responsible practices in the artisan and small-scale miners (ASM) gold sectors of High-Risk and Conflict-Affected Areas (CAHRAs) via a pilot project in Côte d’Ivoire. To do this, the project partners will test an open-pipe ASM gold supply chain model. It will build on the gains made through the Just Gold project in Cote d’Ivoire, established by IMPACT, COOPEDA and SICOM.Participation in the pilot will be enabled via a set of carefully selected digital and non-digital tools that have already been tested by IMPACT and Solidaridad. These tools facilitate the sharing of data to demonstrate responsible trading practices, all the while delivering tangible, timely and relevant rewards and incentives to encourage ongoing participation of both men and women in the upstream supply chain.Throughout the pilot, the lessons learned will carefully document with due consideration of gender both about the specific role of traders in the supply chain and the specific tools that are tested, so that these can inform scaling efforts of other responsible sourcing initiatives in Cote d’Ivoire and elsewhere.Engagement throughout the project with downstream actors, including an London Bullion Market Association (LBMA) refiner involved in the Just Gold project in Cote d’Ivoire, will ensure that the tools deployed in the field meet market demand for due diligence data. Further, learnings and recommendations will also be shared with the Government of Cote d’Ivoire, as well as European Union (EU) governments looking to support responsible sourcing and trade in CAHRAs, as to how a better enabling environment could be created for all traders and miners– with due consideration of gender – to implement responsible practices and engage formal sales channels for ASM gold.
